Q5233.L1t: The Apple iMac is a line of all-in-one desktop computers that has been sold in a range of designs since 1998.
Q5233.L2t: The first colorful iMac G3 models, released in 1999, were sold in a series of fruit-flavored colors.
Q5233.L3t: The fruit-flavored iMac G3 colors included several berry and citrus shades, but the green shade was named lime rather than the fruit named in the option.
Q5233.L4t: Kiwi was not one of the iMac colors, so it is the one that does not belong in the list.
Q5233.L2f: The fruit-named iMac color series was introduced in the early 2010s alongside the first aluminum iMac models.
Q5233.L3f: Tangerine was never used as an iMac color name, as the orange shade was sold under a different name.
Q5233.L4f: Tangerine is the color that was never offered on the iMac, so it is the exception.

Q5731.L1t: Future interests in property law include remainders and executory interests, which are classified by when and how they take effect.
Q5731.L2t: An estate pur autre vie is an estate whose duration is measured by the life of someone other than the holder.
Q5731.L3t: The brother's interest would cut short the uncle's life estate by taking effect on a condition (the uncle moving), and a future interest that divests a prior estate in this way, rather than waiting for it to end naturally, cannot be a remainder.
Q5731.L4t: Because the brother's interest takes effect by divesting the uncle's estate upon his move, it is a shifting executory interest.
Q5731.L2f: At common law, an estate pur autre vie could not be created by a deed and required a will to take effect.
Q5731.L3f: The brother's interest follows the prior estates and is subject to an uncertain condition precedent, and any future interest following a life estate that is not yet certain to vest is classified as a remainder.
Q5731.L4f: The brother's interest is best described as a contingent remainder because it depends on the uncertain event of the uncle moving.

Q5347.L1t: Skeletal muscle contraction is powered by energy from ATP, which is regenerated through several metabolic pathways.
Q5347.L2t: Muscle cells store only a small amount of ATP, and phosphocreatine and glycolysis supply additional energy as activity continues.
Q5347.L3t: The very first energy used in a brief maximal contraction is whatever is already present in the muscle and directly usable, before any regeneration pathway has had time to start.
Q5347.L4t: The initial energy for a very high force contraction lasting 1-2 seconds comes from the ATP already stored in the muscle.
Q5347.L2f: Muscle fibers hold large ATP reserves that can power maximal contractions for about a minute before other pathways are needed.
Q5347.L3f: Even in the first second of a maximal contraction, muscle ATP is used up almost instantly, so the first energy must come from breaking down glucose through the glycolytic pathway.
Q5347.L4f: The initial energy for a very high force contraction lasting 1-2 seconds comes from glycolysis.
